description:
## Outcome

The Mix application version is the only Jido release version source. CLI output, cache paths, run manifests, artifact names, tags, and release metadata read that value.

## Why now

`mix.exs` and `lib/jido_cli/cli.ex` each contain `0.1.0`. The duplicate value can make a tag, command, package, and manifest disagree.

## Work

1. Add a small release identity boundary that reads the compiled application version.
2. Remove the CLI version constant and update `jido --version`, escript cache naming, and automation manifests.
3. Make documentation source references and later package scripts use the same source.
4. Add a tag validator for exact `v<application-version>` agreement.
5. Report the Jido version, Jidoka version, Elixir version, and OTP version through one tested runtime API.
6. Add an architecture test that rejects a second product SemVer literal in production source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mix.exs` owns the only Jido product version value.
- [ ] `jido --version` and JSONL manifest version fields match the application version.
- [ ] A mismatched release tag fails before build or publication.
- [ ] Source, escript, and release builds report the same value.
- [ ] Tests can inject version data without changing global application state.

## Tests

Extend CLI and automation plan tests. Run `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not create a second version file. Do not infer the version from Git at runtime. Protocol schema versions remain separate integers.
title: Make the Mix application version the only release version source
